_comment: Corrections for rows that are wrong in the AccessMedicine source itself. Key = analyte name as produced by parse_lab_values, or 'Name@specimen' (e.g. 'Norepinephrine@plasma') when several rows share the name; 'set' = fields of the Analyte model to overwrite (intervals as {lower_limit, upper_limit}); 'why' = the evidence. Applied before the factor consistency check, so a correction must make the row consistent with its own reference intervals.

Urea nitrogen (BUN).why: Source prints 0.0357, but its own intervals (8-23 mg/dL = 2.9-8.2 mmol/L) and the molar mass of urea nitrogen (2 x 14.007 g/mol -> 10/28.014 = 0.357) give 0.357.

Acetylcholinesterase.why: Source prints U/mL -> U/L with factor 1 and the same interval (5-10) on both sides, but 1 U/mL = 1000 U/L. Factor 1 and the interval are right for kU/L.

Norepinephrine@plasma.why: Source prints nmol/L, but factor 5.91 = 1000/169.18 g/mol converts pg/mL to pmol/L, and its own interval (110-410 pg/mL = 650-2423) only fits pmol/L (as the source itself uses for epinephrine).

Cystine.why: Source prints 83.3 (0.40-1.40 mg/dL = 33-117 μmol/L), which is 10000/120.15 g/mol and counts half-cystine residues. The matched LOINC terms (2177-4, 22672-0) are cystine, the dimer of 240.30 g/mol: 10000/240.30 = 41.6, i.e. half the molar amount (17-58 μmol/L).

Vitamin D, 1,25-dihydroxyvitamin D.why: Source prints 2.6 (16-65 pg/mL = 42-169 pmol/L), which is 1000/384.6 g/mol, the molar mass of vitamin D3 without hydroxyl groups. Calcitriol has 416.64 g/mol: 1000/416.64 = 2.40 (16-65 pg/mL = 38-156 pmol/L).

Alanine aminotransferase (ALT, SGPT).why: Source leaves this enzyme in U/L (factor 1) while it converts aspartate aminotransferase, creatine kinase, amylase and the other enzymes to μKat/L. Same conversion applied, with the exact factor 1/60 = 0.01667: 10-40 U/L = 0.17-0.67 μKat/L.

Alkaline phosphatase.why: As for alanine aminotransferase: the source leaves it in U/L. 50-120 U/L = 0.83-2.0 μKat/L.

Lactate dehydrogenase (LDH).why: As for alanine aminotransferase: the source leaves it in U/L. 50-200 U/L = 0.83-3.33 μKat/L.

Lamotrigine.why: Source prints μg/dL, but factor 3.91 = 1000/256.1 g/mol converts μg/mL to μmol/L, and 2.5-15 μg/mL is the therapeutic range.

Glucose-6-phosphate dehydrogenase.why: Source prints U/mol Hb with factor 0.0645, but 1 U/g Hb x 64500 g/mol = 64500 U/mol Hb = 0.0645 MU/mol Hb.

Whole blood.why: The HbA1c row of the source carries its specimen ('Whole blood') as name because the group header is not indented. Factor 1 for '% of total Hb' -> 'Fraction of total Hb' is wrong: 4-5.6 % is 0.04-0.056 as a fraction, so the factor is 0.01 (as the source itself uses for methemoglobin).

Hemoglobin A2.why: Factor 1 for '% total Hb' -> 'Fraction of 1.0' is wrong: 2.0-3.5 % is 0.020-0.035 as a fraction, so the factor is 0.01.

Hemoglobin F (fetal hemoglobin in adult).why: Source prints the SI interval as '<2' although the unit is 'Fraction of total Hb' and the factor 0.01 is correct: <2 % is <0.02.

Amino acid fractionation, Cystine.why: Second listing of cystine; same correction as 'Cystine' (dimer, 240.30 g/mol).

Anion gap (Na+)−(Cl− + HCO3−).why: Source prints nmol/L, but 8-16 mEq/L with factor 1 is 8-16 mmol/L.

Differential count (absolute), Neutrophi.why: Source prints factor 1 for μL−1 -> 10^9 L−1, but 1/μL is 10^6/L = 0.001 x 10^9/L, as its own intervals show (e.g. neutrophils 1800-7800 /μL = 1.8-7.8 x 10^9/L).

Lidocaine (therapeutic).why: Source prints the garbled unit 'μmL g/mL'; factor 4.27 = 1000/234.34 g/mol converts μg/mL to μmol/L.

Oxazepam (therapeutic).why: Source prints the SI interval as 0.7-54.9, but 1.4 μg/mL x 3.49 = 4.9 μmol/L.

Protein electrophoresis (SPEP), concentr.why: Source prints the SI interval as 1-10, but 0.1-0.4 g/dL x 10 = 1-4 g/L.

Bilirubin, Total.why: Source prints the SI interval as 2-18, but 0.3-1.2 mg/dL x 17.1 = 5-21 μmol/L. The factor is right: bilirubin has 584.66 g/mol, 10000/584.66 = 17.1.

Desipramine (therapeutic).why: Source prints the SI interval as 170-700, but 50-200 ng/mL x 3.75 = 188-750 nmol/L. The factor is right: desipramine has 266.38 g/mol, 1000/266.38 = 3.75.

Estradiol (unconjugated), male.why: Source prints the SI interval as <184, but <20 pg/mL x 3.67 = <73 pmol/L.

Pregnanediol, female, Luteal phase.why: Source prints the SI interval as 8-33, but 2.3 mg/24 h x 3.12 = 7.2 μmol/day. The factor is right: pregnanediol has 320.51 g/mol, 1000/320.51 = 3.12.

MCH, substance concentration, Hb [Fe].why: LOINC models the red cell indices as properties of the red cells (SYSTEM = RBC), although they are measured in a whole blood sample, which is what the source names.

Ammonia (as NH3).why: Source prints 0.714 = 10/14.007, the factor for ammonia expressed as nitrogen, but labels the row 'as NH3'. Ammonia has 17.031 g/mol: 10/17.031 = 0.587 (15-50 μg/dL = 9-29 μmol/L).

Bupropion (Wellbutrin, Zyban).why: Source prints 3.62 = 1000/276.2, the molar mass of bupropion hydrochloride. A plasma concentration is that of bupropion itself, 239.74 g/mol: 1000/239.74 = 4.17 (25-100 ng/mL = 104-417 nmol/L).

Alanine (adult).why: Source prints μmol/day for a plasma concentration; its second alanine row has μmol/L.
